firstMessage.rawMarkdown:
(Even though my score is still very mediocre, per the private sharing rules of Kaggle I think I will still need to write something here)

There was an Autoresearch Systems Hackathon [today](https://luma.com/fvz1h1dq?tk=3suiEk).
I participated.
I worked on agentically finding a model architecture that can curve-fit ARC-AGI-3 actions.

I got third place. The prize was $1,000 of Modal credits, and $1,000 of ChatGPT credits, and 6 months of ChatGPT Pro.

This is the script to the [video](https://youtu.be/IX8skOPlX_A) I submitted for judging.

```plaintext
[show sp80 gameplay]
I am working ARC-AGI-3.
ARC-AGI-3 contains games that humans can easily solve, but not AI.
Today, I am using autoresearch to find a model architecture could learn how to play games.

[scorecard view]
I already have a dataset of hundreds of ideal gameplays.

[loss view]
The dataset is used to train the model.

[model view]
So today, I made an autoresearch agent to find the best model architecture.
You can see that the agent is trying out different ideas to minimize validation loss.

[frontier view]
This is the autoresearch graph you might be familiar with.
As you can see this, we get improved validation loss as autoresearch progresses.

[modal]
This is possible with Modal compute, as the agent can train 10 experiments in parallel, each with a GPU.

[submission page]
I am making submissions to Kaggle, where the ARC-AGI contest is held.
```

I also gave a live presentation, which is pretty much the same content.

This is the GitHub [repository](https://github.com/tonghuikang/arc3) that I made available to the judges. The "autoresearch" dash is [here](http://tonghuikang.github.io/arc3/training/metrics.html). I wrote a [blog post](https://blog.huikang.dev/2026/05/31/autoresearch-hackathon.html).
